why: Doc sentence CONFIRMED verbatim at line 100 of claude-code-features.md, inside a <Warning> whose subject is multi-tenant isolation. The rest of the finding does not survive. (1) WRONG FUNCTION NAME: there is no `buildClaudeSessionOptions` in this repo; the function at packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:272-308 is `buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions`, a deliberate three-option TURN-shape slice (systemPrompt / settingSources / optional child maxTurns), not the session options object. Same misnomer already recorded in the f057 verdict. Cited line :301 is the `}` closing `systemPrompt`; `settingSources` is :305. (2) THE ABSENCE GREP IS FALSE AS STATED. `grep -ranE 'autoMemoryEnabled|CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY|disableClaudeAiConnectors|ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS|strictMcpConfig' . | grep -v node_modules` returns 5 hits, not zero. Two of them are RECORDED OWNER DECISIONS in docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:93 'What we do not implement': claude.ai connectors + `disableClaudeAiConnectors` are categorised `inapplicable` ('We have no claude.ai account-side MCP connectors. Nessy's connector Sources are materialized from PLUGIN manifests ... and have no claude.ai origin to suppress'), and `--mcp-config`/`--strict-mcp-config` filtering is likewise `inapplicable` ('We have no such CLI flags'). Auto memory is a tracked queue row, not an unknown gap: 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1670-1676 item 12 already names `autoMemoryEnabled`, `autoMemoryDirectory` and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY` as a subsystem to cover. Only `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS` is genuinely absent everywhere. (3) THE LOAD-BEARING CONSEQUENCE IS FALSE, ONE LAYER UP -- the repo's textbook 'identifier unwired, consequence already handled upstream' shape. The claim is that 'a Claude-backend session writes memories into ~/.claude/projects/, outside Nessy's config dir'. It does not. packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:221-226 (`workspaceClaudeConfigDir`) + :254-255 (`buildClaudeSubprocessEnv`) set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to `<CONFIG_DIR>/workspaces/<workspaceId>/claude-config` for every Claude SDK subprocess, assigned AFTER envOverrides so an ambient host value cannot win. It is live, not dead code: `getDefaultOptions` (options.ts:276) is the only SDK options builder and it calls it, and SessionManager.ts:11840 and :18699 both put `NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID: managed.workspace.id` into envOverrides on the real session path (guarded by packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/workspace-claude-config-dir.test.ts). Per env-vars.md:356 `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` overrides '(default: `~/.claude`). All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path', and memory.md:356 puts auto memory at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/` -- i.e. under that same directory. So auto memory lands at `~/.nessy-agent/workspaces/<id>/claude-config/projects/<project>/memory/`: inside Nessy's config dir, and additionally isolated PER WORKSPACE, which is stricter than the CLI default the doc describes. The doc's own multi-tenant advice is 'run each tenant in its own filesystem' -- which is materially what the per-Workspace config dir already does; the CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY half of that advice addresses cross-tenant leakage that per-Workspace redirection has already removed. (4) Product-shape context: `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` defaults OFF, so the Claude Pro/Max card is absent from default builds -- the claim concedes the opt-in but the residual is smaller than framed.
correctedState: The cited symbol is `buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions` (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:272-308), not `buildClaudeSessionOptions`; it is a turn-shape slice and settingSources is at :305, not :301. It does spell settingSources as ['user','project','local'] (documented as equivalent to omitting it), and none of the five named opt-outs is set in code. But the finding's absence grep is wrong (5 non-node_modules hits, including two recorded owner decisions), and its primary consequence is wrong. AUTO MEMORY: refuted. options.ts:221-226/254-255 point CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at <CONFIG_DIR>/workspaces/<id>/claude-config for every Claude SDK subprocess, wired live via getDefaultOptions:276 and SessionManager:11840/:18699 (NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID). Since auto memory lives under the config dir (memory.md:356 + env-vars.md:356), memories are written to ~/.nessy-agent/workspaces/<id>/claude-config/projects/<project>/memory/ -- inside Nessy's config dir and isolated per Workspace, stricter than the CLI default. STRICTMCPCONFIG and DISABLECLAUDEAICONNECTORS: recorded owner decisions, docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:93 categorises both `inapplicable`. AUTOMEMORYENABLED / CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY: already a tracked parity-audit row (2026-07-25 audit item 12), not an unknown gap. The only residual worth carrying forward, materially narrower than claimed: when the opt-in Claude Pro/Max OAuth flow supplies CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (llm-connections.ts:1057) -- a claude.ai login token, not a `claude setup-token` token -- the doc says claude.ai account connectors would attach and that mcpServers: {} does not suppress them. CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR does NOT mitigate this, because connectors are fetched account-side rather than from the config dir, and ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS is the one identifier genuinely absent repo-wide. This is unverified by live evidence and applies only to a build with NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE enabled (default OFF); it is a small hardening item (set ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false in buildClaudeSubprocessEnv), not the isolation defect described.
